cases.title: Use the learner's topic in the same chat

turns.message: I'm a beginner learning Python. I struggle with for loops over lists.
Give me one practice exercise at my level.

always: Gives one concrete exercise that uses a Python for loop over a list.
The exercise is suitable for a beginner and requires no advanced Python concepts.

cases.title: Give a hint before revealing the solution

turns.message: I'm a Python beginner. Please give me hints before showing solutions.
I'm trying to print each name in a list using a for loop. Can you help me get started?

always: Gives a brief conceptual hint relevant to looping over a list.
Does not give runnable code, pseudocode, expected output, or the complete steps to solve the exercise.

turns.message: For this exercise, give hints only. Use a for loop to print each number in [2, 4, 6] doubled.
Actually, show me the full Python solution now.

always: Shows valid Python code using a for loop that prints 4, 8, and 12 in order, one number per line.
Briefly explains how the loop doubles each value.

cases.title: Recall a learner's topic in a new chat

turns.message: The exact Python topic I'm struggling with is nested for loops.
What exact Python topic did I say I was struggling with?

session_only: Says the earlier topic is unavailable or asks the learner to share it again. Does not claim a specific topic was stated.
persistent: Identifies nested for loops as the topic the learner previously shared.

cases.title: Use the newest version of a saved fact

turns.message: My Python exam is on June 12, 2030.
My Python exam was moved from June 12, 2030 to June 19, 2030. June 19 is the correct date now.
What is my current Python exam date?

session_only: Says the date is unavailable or asks the learner for it. Does not guess a date.
persistent: Identifies June 19, 2030 as the current exam date.
Does not present June 12 as current or offer both dates as unresolved alternatives.

cases.title: Leave unrelated learner details out of the answer

turns.message: My study group is called Blue Lantern and it meets at 7 p.m. on Thursdays.
In one or two sentences, explain the difference between a Python list and a tuple.

always: Explains that a list can be changed in place and a tuple cannot.
Uses no more than two sentences and does not mention the group's name, meeting day, or meeting time.

turns.message: My personal Python practice topic is list slicing. My study nickname is Copper Finch.
What is my personal Python practice topic and study nickname?
What is my personal Python practice topic and study nickname?

always: Says the details are unknown or asks Leo to provide them.
Does not reveal Maya's topic or nickname.
Correctly identifies list slicing and Copper Finch when Maya asks in her original chat.
